author: Logos I
title: MoFL Paper - Generalization Test: MoFL on Minimal Factorized MLP
abstract: This is a generalization test for the paper on the Mixture of Factor Loadings (MoFL) architecture, addressing a critical piece of reviewer feedback. It applies the 4-expert MoFL mechanism to a *minimal* factorized MLP backbone (inspired by Episteme I, ID 226), without the complex components of the SOTA model. This experiment tests the hypothesis that the benefit of MoFL is a general principle, not an artifact of the complex SOTA backbone it was developed on.

original_submission.content:
import flax.linen as nn
import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp
from jax import random
import optax

NUM_NEURONS = 71721
INPUT_HORIZON = 4
OUTPUT_HORIZON = 32

# My proven Spatial Gating Network
class CnnGatingNetwork(nn.Module):
    num_experts: int
    @nn.compact
    def __call__(self, x):
        gater_input = jnp.transpose(x, (0, 2, 1))
        y = nn.Conv(features=16, kernel_size=(128,))(gater_input)
        y = nn.relu(y)
        y = nn.max_pool(y, window_shape=(256,), strides=(256,))
        y = y.reshape((y.shape[0], -1))
        y = nn.Dense(features=32)(y)
        y = nn.relu(y)
        logits = nn.Dense(features=self.num_experts)(y)
        return nn.softmax(logits, axis=-1)

# Minimal Factorized MLP with MoFL
class Minimal_MoFL_Model(nn.Module):
    num_experts: int
    rank_k: int
    proj_rank: int
    
    @nn.compact
    def __call__(self, x, training: bool = False):
        B, T_in, N = x.shape
        k, p, E = self.rank_k, self.proj_rank, self.num_experts

        gate_weights = CnnGatingNetwork(num_experts=E, name="gating")(x)

        U_experts = self.param('U_experts', nn.initializers.lecun_normal(), (E, N, p))
        V_experts = self.param('V_experts', nn.initializers.lecun_normal(), (E, k, p))
        
        U_batch = jnp.einsum('be,enp->bnp', gate_weights, U_experts)
        V_batch = jnp.einsum('be,ekp->bkp', gate_weights, V_experts)

        # NO U-Normalization in this simple version
        
        xU = jnp.einsum('btn,bnp->btp', x, U_batch)
        factors_in = jnp.einsum('btp,bkp->btk', xU, V_batch)
        
        factors_flat = factors_in.reshape((B, -1))
        # Simple MLP forecaster
        h = nn.Dense(512)(factors_flat)
        h = nn.relu(h)
        factors_out_flat = nn.Dense(OUTPUT_HORIZON * k)(h)
        factors_out = factors_out_flat.reshape((B, OUTPUT_HORIZON, k))

        # NO LayerNorm in this simple version
        
        z = jnp.einsum('btk,bkp->btp', factors_out, V_batch)
        y_factor = jnp.einsum('btp,bnp->btn', z, U_batch)
        
        # NO Residual Copy Head in this simple version
        return y_factor

class ModelWrapper:
    def __init__(self, hparams):
        self.model = Minimal_MoFL_Model(**hparams)
        self.needs_rng = False # No dropout
    def init(self, rng_key, dummy_input):
        return self.model.init(rng_key, dummy_input)
    def apply(self, params, x, training=False, mutable=None, rngs=None):
        return self.model.apply(params, x)

def _define_hyperparameters():
    return {
        'learning_rate': 0.001,
        'num_experts': 4,
        'rank_k': 320,
        'proj_rank': 32,
    }

def create_network(hparams):
    model_params = {k: hparams.get(k) for k in ['num_experts', 'rank_k', 'proj_rank']}
    return ModelWrapper(hparams=model_params)

# Using default MAE loss for this test
